content:
Recently, I visited the Office of the Director General of Police, Gujarat State, in connection with a client's matter involving a bank account that had been subjected to restrictions in relation to a cyber fraud investigation.
The client's bank account came under scrutiny after certain transactions were linked to an ongoing cyber fraud investigation. As part of the preventive measures adopted during such investigations, restrictions were placed on the account pending verification by the concerned authorities.
The client maintained that they had no knowledge, involvement, or participation in any fraudulent activity. However, the account restriction caused significant inconvenience and affected the client's ability to carry out regular financial transactions.

I personally visited the Office of the Director General of Police, Gujarat State, in connection with the matter and submitted a detailed representation along with relevant documents, transaction records, and supporting materials for examination.
The client's explanation and the complete transaction trail were placed before the concerned authorities for appropriate consideration. The representation sought a proper review of the circumstances in which the account had been restricted and requested necessary action in accordance with the applicable legal and administrative procedure.
The matter also involved coordination with the concerned banking authorities and nodal officers so that the account restriction could be examined on the basis of the available records and the client's explanation.

Where applicable, matters involving NCRP/CFCFRMS-related transactions require proper examination of the money trail, the underlying complaint, and the role of each account appearing in the transaction chain.

It is important to understand that an account appearing in a cyber fraud transaction trail does not, by itself, establish that the account holder participated in the alleged fraud. The circumstances of the transaction and the account holder's role require proper examination by the concerned authorities.

If Your Bank Account Has Been Frozen
If your bank account has been subjected to a debit freeze, lien mark, transaction hold, or other restriction in connection with a cyber fraud complaint:
Do not panic or ignore the restriction.
Preserve bank statements and complete transaction records.
Identify the NCRP/complaint reference, if available.
Cooperate with the investigating agency.
Provide genuine documents explaining the source and nature of the transaction.
Submit a proper representation before the concerned authority and bank/nodal officer.
Seek timely legal assistance where the restriction continues without resolution.

comment: A key operational challenge is ensuring timely communication between banks, nodal officers and investigators. Delays in verification can create hardship even when the transaction trail ultimately clears the account holder.
